steps.title: API streams reconstructed bytes to client
steps.action: Coordinator delivers the reconstructed 10 MB chunk to the API, which pipes it through TLS back to the client. For multi-chunk objects, the API pipelines chunks so the client starts receiving bytes before all chunks are fully read.
steps.codeOrCommand:
response.headers["Content-Length"] = row.size_bytes
response.headers["ETag"] = row.etag
response.headers["x-amz-version-id"] = row.version_id
for chunk in row.chunks: bytes = repl.read_and_decode(chunk) response.write(bytes) # streamed
response.end

steps.title: LB streams response back
steps.action: LB just relays TCP bytes; no buffering for large streams (would blow LB memory at fleet scale).

steps.title: Client receives bytes, verifies ETag
steps.action: SDK streams to disk, computes MD5 as it goes, compares with Content-ETag on completion. End-to-end GET latency for a 10 MB object: ~60–120ms hot, ~200–400ms if any shards need NVMe reads.

operations.title: DELETE object (tombstone + async GC)
operations.name: DELETE object (tombstone + async GC)
operations.description: User deletes an object. API writes a tombstone row in metadata — the delete is visible immediately, but the underlying chunks are reclaimed later by the garbage collector.

steps.title: Client issues DELETE
steps.action: Signed DELETE request on the key. No body.
steps.codeOrCommand:
DELETE /my-bucket/logs/old-2024.log HTTP/1.1
Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256...

steps.title: LB forwards to API
steps.action: Least-connections; DELETE is stateless and idempotent.

steps.title: Auth validates s3:DeleteObject
steps.action: SigV4 + policy check. Deletes often require an explicit allow — default-deny on destructive ops.
steps.codeOrCommand:
assert verify_sigv4(req)
assert evaluate(policies, op="s3:DeleteObject") == "Allow"

steps.title: API writes tombstone (logical delete)
steps.action: Rather than deleting the row, API inserts a new version marked tombstone=true. This is cheap (one row write) and makes deletes idempotent.
steps.codeOrCommand:
version_id = uuid7
meta.insert_tombstone( bucket="my-bucket", key="logs/old-2024.log", version_id=version_id, deleted_at=now, actor="arn:aws:iam::1234:user/alice"
)
# old version rows remain; versioning-enabled buckets can restore by omitting the tombstone

steps.title: Metadata commits tombstone row
steps.action: Single-row insert; linearizable. The moment this commits, subsequent GETs return 404 — the actual shards are untouched on disk.
steps.codeOrCommand:
INSERT INTO objects (bucket, key, version_id, tombstone, deleted_at, chunks)
VALUES ('my-bucket', 'logs/old-2024.log', '01HZ8TD-ver00-del', true, now, null);

steps.title: Versioning log records the tombstone
steps.action: Append to the event stream; GC subscribes to this topic to schedule chunk reclamation after the grace window.
steps.codeOrCommand:
producer.send( topic="object-events", key="my-bucket/logs/old-2024.log", value={ "ts": "2026-04-24T10:16:42Z", "op": "DELETE", "bucket": "my-bucket", "key": "logs/old-2024.log", "version_id": "01HZ8TD-ver00-del", "grace_expires_at": "2026-05-01T10:16:42Z" }
)

steps.title: API returns 204 No Content
steps.action: Deletes are idempotent — deleting an already-deleted key also returns 204. Total user-facing DELETE latency: ~10–20ms (one metadata write + auth).
steps.codeOrCommand: return Response(204, headers={"x-amz-delete-marker": "true", "x-amz-version-id": "01HZ8TD-ver00-del"})

steps.title: Client receives 204
steps.action: Delete is durable and visible. Physical bytes still on data nodes until GC runs.

steps.title: Garbage collector (much later) sweeps expired tombstones
steps.action: Background worker scans tombstones past the 7-day grace window. For each, it looks up the chunk list from the prior version and schedules shard deletion on each data node.
steps.codeOrCommand:
# Runs continuously, throttled to 10% disk I/O
for event in log.consume(topic="object-events", filter="op=DELETE"): if event.grace_expires_at > now: continue # too early prior = meta.get_version_before(event.version_id) if prior is None: continue for chunk in prior.chunks: for shard in chunk.shards: data_node_rpc.quarantine(shard.node, chunk.chunk_id, shard.shard_idx, release_at=now + 24h) meta.purge_versions_for(event.bucket, event.key, older_than=event.ts)
steps.decision: Two-phase delete: shards go into 24h quarantine before physical removal. A stale metadata lookup during quarantine can still read the shard — prevents correctness bugs from eating data.

steps.title: Data nodes physically delete shards after quarantine
steps.action: After the 24h quarantine, each data node marks the extent region as free; the on-disk bytes are overwritten by the next append or by background compaction.
steps.codeOrCommand:
# On each data node
for shard in quarantined_shards_ready: extent_index.delete(f"{shard.chunk_id}:{shard.shard_idx}") extent.punch_hole(ref.offset, ref.length) # FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE metrics.reclaimed_bytes.inc(ref.length)
steps.note: Hole-punching returns space to the filesystem without rewriting the extent; log-structured storage reclaims large contiguous free regions via background compaction.

tradeoffs.rationale: Gets 11 nines at ~1.5x storage vs. 3x for full replication. Costs more CPU on the read path and makes single-shard recovery slower than a simple copy.

tradeoffs.chosen: Strongly-consistent metadata service, dumb bulk-storage data nodes
tradeoffs.rationale: Lets each plane scale on its own axis: metadata is CPU and index-bound, data nodes are disk-bound. Also keeps the consistency surface tiny and well-defined.
Returns instantly, is idempotent under retries, and plays well with versioning. Costs disk space until the GC sweeps, which is acceptable at EB scale.

tradeoffs.chosen: Multipart with client-chosen part size (5-100 MB)
tradeoffs.rationale: Parallelism saturates the client uplink and lets single-part failures retry cheaply. Adds an explicit Complete step, which the SDK hides.

tradeoffs.chosen: Strongly consistent, paginated with continuation tokens
